title: Adaptive league full-network representation pilot
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The frozen representation is the remaining bottleneck: small-step all-street PPO across the full network can learn more general state features than head-only updates, while stronger exact-source KL and a tighter PPO KL gate prevent destructive drift.
material_change: Resume Standard10; reset optimizer/hand counter; train full network on all streets at lr 3e-6; source KL 3; target KL 0.005; advantage clip 3; same adaptive three-opponent league and 25% self-play; separate preflop head retained but trainable.
baseline: All-policy-heads predecessor completed 263602 hands and strongly beat Slumbot-free, but iter32 confirmation lower bounds were negative vs Standard10 and CFR96. Head-only capacity is exhausted without robust promotion.

notes: Preregistered smoke gate: finite changes in representation and both policy heads, ref-KL safely below 0.005, no KL stop/PPO clipping/action collapse, valid assignment provenance. Production is forbidden if preflop distribution or ratio tails become abnormal.
Smoke gate PASS: all representation and head tensors changed by finite small amounts (max abs 6.2e-6), ref-KL 3.8e-5 << 0.005, no PPO clipping/KL stop/action collapse, assignment chain valid.
Smoke passed strict trust-region and parameter-change gates; launch fixed 262144-hand production from original Standard10, not from smoke.
Production iter16 archive retained. Full-network movement remains below tighter KL gate; low-frequency PPO clipping is present but action ratios and distributions remain healthy.
Production iter32 halfway archive retained. Representation learning remains below 0.005 KL gate; transient drift reversed without intervention.
Production iter48 archive retained. Full-network representation learning remains inside the tighter KL gate with low PPO clipping and stable action distributions.

result.summary: Full-network all-street league training completed 263410 production hands with stable KL health and positive league reward. Nevertheless, every frozen archive lost to Standard10 on the fixed three-anchor discovery curve and CFR96 was mostly negative/high-variance; no confirmation or Slumbot run was launched.
result.conclusion: Representation learning increased policy movement without producing robust strength. On-policy PPO league reward is not sufficiently correlated with frozen-policy performance in this high-variance poker setting; expanding trainable capacity is not the limiting factor.
result.next_step: Stop widening or extending unchanged PPO. Reassess AlphaHoldem-style variance reduction and credit assignment using existing trainer capabilities and primary paper evidence; choose a bounded causal control before more environment-scale training.
